definition: Week 1 model-vs-market audit after validated QB reconciliation and current 2026 team-strength review. Diagnostic layer only; not an official betting card.

games.auditConclusion: Small Seattle lean only; no reason to force before final availability.
Rams lean survives numerically, but Melbourne travel and current availability widen the error band.

QB reconciliation moved fair value toward Tampa rather than Cincinnati. Current 2026 evidence is genuinely split: Cincinnati projects as a top-tier offense but still a bottom-tier defense, while Tampa has a top-two OL and a stronger defensive outlook. Do not manually force the rating toward market; test offense-vs-defense prior weighting first.

The gap survives validated QB reconciliation. Buffalo projects as an elite offense with a weak defense; Houston projects as the league's top defense but a bottom-third offense. This is now an offense-vs-defense weighting audit, not a Josh Allen pricing problem.

QB corrections nearly cancel, but current team evidence strongly favors Baltimore beyond the existing BAL -0.5 line: Baltimore projects top-10 offensively and top-five defensively, while Indianapolis is closer to mid/lower-tier offense and defense despite an elite OL. Rebase the non-QB team prior before considering IND +3.5.

Direction remains strongly supported because Cleveland projects last offensively and near-bottom defensively after losing Garrett/Schwartz. However Jacksonville's own OL ranks near the bottom and its offense is closer to mid-pack, so the JAX -12+ model state should carry a wide uncertainty band rather than automatic confidence.
Validated QB scenarios put Pittsburgh roughly -2.4 to -3.1 versus market -3. Prior Pittsburgh edge is effectively gone until Atlanta names its starter.
QB reconciliation reduced the theoretical Arizona edge to roughly two points. Remains research only.
Raiders QB reconciliation already flipped the baseline toward Las Vegas before assigning Malik Willis a full value. Original Miami edge is invalidated.
Kyler Murray transition moved the QB-reconciled model to roughly MIN -2 versus market -1.5. Prior Green Bay edge is eliminated.
Philadelphia lean remains below the high-priority threshold and requires final availability review.
Dallas offensive continuity remains stronger than the old baseline reversal implied. Keep Giants edge blocked until non-QB team prior is rebuilt.

Healthy Mahomes calibration does not explain the market gap. Current 2026 unit evidence favors Kansas City much more strongly than the near-pick'em model: KC projects top-10 on offense, defense and OL, while Denver is elite on OL/defense but only mid-tier offensively. Requires non-QB structural rebase; DEN +3 remains blocked.

nextCalibration: Separate prior-season offense and defense predictive weights are being backtested before any manual team-rating correction is allowed.
